GM.thesis_one_line: America's #2 automaker, priced by the market for stagnation while its own guidance keeps rising and its core auto business is net-cash, not net-debt.
kill_criteria: Adjusted EBIT-adjusted guidance cut (vs the current $14.0–16.0bn FY26 range) at any of the next two quarterly releases.
Automotive segment swings from net-cash to net-debt positive (i.e., Automotive debt exceeds Automotive cash+securities) for two consecutive quarters.
Gross tariff-cost estimate re-raised above the current $2.5–3.5bn 2026 range.
Two consecutive quarters of GAAP-to-adjusted EBIT gap driven by *new* (not previously disclosed) restructuring/impairment charges exceeding $1bn/quarter.
China equity income (currently modestly positive, $83M in Q2 2026) turns negative for two consecutive quarters.
key_adverse_facts: FY2025 GAAP diluted EPS was $3.27 vs the original guidance range of $8.30-9.05, due to a $7.2bn Q4 2025 EV-realignment charge.
China JV restructuring charges are recurring ($99M six-month 2026).
Cruise robotaxi business was wound down after >$10bn cumulative spend (Dec 2024) - a past capital-allocation miss.
Automotive-only balance sheet split and TTM adjusted-EBIT reconstruction were derived via automated summarization of primary SEC documents, not a full manual read of every table.
data_conflicts: V1 rates GM 'excessive' using TTM GAAP EBIT ($1.815bn, 0.98% margin, depressed by one-off EV/China charges) and consolidated net debt ($104bn, ~90% GM Financial captive debt). On GM's own adjusted EBIT ($14.42bn TTM, 7.8% margin) and automotive-only net cash (~$8.7bn net cash per the Q2 2026 10-Q balance sheet, not net debt), GM's EV/adjusted-EBIT is ~4.6x, implying a near-zero-to-negative perpetual growth rate priced in - i.e. cheap, not excessive.

confidence_in_thesis.reason: Primary-source SEC filings were cross-checked (TTM revenue independently matches the D3 dataset's figure); the automotive/GM Financial debt split is taken directly from the 10-Q balance sheet. Some figures were extracted via automated document summarization rather than a full manual read, and the sum-of-parts EV used to challenge V1 is a simplification, not a full independent valuation model.

valuation_view_vs_v1.reconciliation: V1's reverse DCF used TTM GAAP EBIT depressed by one-off EV/China restructuring charges and a consolidated net-debt figure dominated by GM Financial's self-funding captive-finance debt. On GM's own adjusted EBIT and an automotive-only (net-cash) balance-sheet view, GM's EV/adjusted-EBIT is roughly 4.6x, implying priced-in growth near zero to negative - the opposite of 'excessive'.

OMC.thesis_one_line: Now the world's largest ad holding company after merging with Interpublic; cheap on depressed post-merger earnings, but integration is only 10 months old.
kill_criteria: Organic growth (Core Ops) falls below 3% for two consecutive quarters.
Net debt / adjusted EBITDA rises above 3.0x (from an estimated ~2x currently) at any quarter-end.
Cumulative disclosed 2026 cost synergies come in below $600M (vs the $900M 2026 target) by year-end.
A second consecutive year of full-year GAAP net income below FY2024's $1.48bn level (i.e., integration costs fail to taper as promised).

Any adverse ruling or expanded damages exposure in the A.A. et al v. Omnicom Group Qatar World Cup migrant-labor 'sportswashing' litigation (S.D.N.Y., 1:25-cv-03389; motions to dismiss for lack of jurisdiction denied in 2026) that a reasonable analyst would judge reputationally or financially material.
key_adverse_facts: FY2025 GAAP net loss of $54.5M (EPS -$0.27) driven by merger/integration costs.
Long-term debt roughly doubled to $9.27bn post-merger (from $6.07bn a year earlier).
A.A. v. Omnicom Qatar World Cup migrant-labor litigation is proceeding; motions to dismiss for lack of jurisdiction were denied in 2026.
FTC consent order imposes ongoing ad-placement documentation and annual-reporting obligations.
data_conflicts: No V1 row exists for OMC, so no V1 conflict. The triage's extreme trailing P/E (205.8x) and 3,074% EPS-growth figures are confirmed here to be merger-accounting/comp-base noise (FY2025 was a GAAP loss year), not real underlying economics.

confidence_in_thesis.reason: The merger closed only 10 months ago, so no full clean annual comparison exists yet. Net debt/EBITDA and a formal three-closest-peer valuation comp were not independently reconstructed at this depth (disclosed as data gaps in the dossier).

valuation_view_vs_v1.reconciliation: No V1 valuation row exists for OMC; not applicable. Using a secondary consensus cross-check only (forward P/E ~7x on FY26 adjusted EPS), the market is pricing in flat-to-low-single-digit growth versus organic growth already running at 6.1% (Q2 2026) plus a disclosed $1.5bn three-year synergy target - i.e., growth priced in looks at or below what is being delivered.

WYNN.thesis_one_line: Macau/Las Vegas luxury casino operator riding a genuine mass-market Macau recovery, but carrying elevated, just-repriced-higher debt into an unproven UAE project.
kill_criteria: Net debt / adjusted EBITDAR rises above 4.5x at any quarter-end (from ~3.7-3.9x currently).

Wynn Al Marjan Island opening slips beyond March 2028 (6+ months past the reaffirmed September 2027 date) or total project cost is disclosed at a level requiring new external financing beyond the existing revolvers.
Las Vegas or Encore Boston Harbor adjusted EBITDAR declines YoY for three consecutive quarters (two already logged in Q2 2026).
Macau mass-market table win percentage at either Wynn Palace or Wynn Macau falls below 20% for two consecutive quarters (Wynn Macau was already 15.1-17.1% in the last two quarters - watch closely).
Any credit-rating downgrade following the September 2026 refinancing, or a covenant-headroom disclosure in the next 10-Q.
key_adverse_facts: September 2026 refinancing raised the coupon on $900M of notes from 5.250% to 6.875%, increasing run-rate interest expense.
Las Vegas and Encore Boston Harbor adjusted EBITDAR both declined YoY in Q2 2026.
Wynn Al Marjan Island (UAE) total project cost is undisclosed; cumulative cash contributions were $1.06bn as of Q2 2026 and rising.
Wynn Macau mass-market table win percentage declined YoY in both of the last two quarters (17.1% vs 17.4%; 15.1% vs 18.7%).
data_conflicts: No V1 row exists for WYNN, so no V1 conflict. The triage's cited 5.7x net debt/EBITDA vs our ~3.7-3.9x EBITDAR-basis estimate is most likely a definitional difference (EBITDAR, pre-rent add-back, vs EBITDA, post-rent), not a factual conflict; not independently reconciled at this depth.

confidence_in_thesis.reason: TTM adjusted EBITDAR and net-leverage figures are estimated from a partial (not full 8-quarter) reconstruction, and Wynn Al Marjan Island's total project cost is an undisclosed material unknown that directly affects the leverage/liquidity outlook.

valuation_view_vs_v1.reconciliation: No V1 valuation row exists for WYNN; not applicable. Secondary consensus price targets (~$135, ~66% above the $81.12 close) suggest the market is pricing in more caution than sell-side models - consistent with 'cheap', though the reservation (leverage, undisclosed UAE cost) is why this is INCLUDE-SMALL rather than full INCLUDE.
